name: Italian Mediterranean buffalo
notes: Mainly Campania; milk for buffalo mozzarella (PDO Mozzarella di Bufala Campana); herd-book opened 1980, officially recognised 2000

name: Nili-Ravi
notes: Punjab region; dairy buffalo; about 2000 kg milk per year

name: Sarda
notes: Sardinia; principal Italian sheep milk breed; milk goes to pecorino sardo and pecorino romano

name: Comisana
notes: Faccia Rossa or Lentinese; Sicily, named for Comiso; herdbook 1976; crossing of Pinzirita and Maltese sheep late 1800s

name: LaMancha
notes: American Lamancha; bred by Eula Fay Frey from about 1927; registered 1958; ear type gopher or elf; Wikipedia title American Lamancha

name: Oberhasli
notes: From Chamois Colored Goat of Oberhasli; all purebreds descend from five goats imported 1936; ADGA accepted breed 1978 or 1979

name: Sahiwal
notes: Zebu; named for Sahiwal District; milk, meat and draught; crossed with Friesian and Jersey

name: Gir
notes: Also Gyr; Kathiawar, Gujarat; Indian Gir about 2110 kg milk per lactation; Brazilian Gir Leiteiro dairy strain since 1960s

name: Red Sindhi
notes: Western Sindh and Las Bela; dairy zebu

name: Tharparkar
notes: Also White Sindhi, Cutchi, Thari; dual-purpose milk and draught

name: Kankrej
notes: Rann of Kutch; Kankaraj in Pakistan; draught and milk

name: Tarentaise
notes: Tarentaise valley; Wikipedia page notes cheese from Tarentaise, Beaufortain and Maurienne but does not name Beaufort

name: Abondance
notes: Haute-Savoie, formerly Chablaisienne; herd-book 1891 (or 1894); about 80% of milk to protected cheeses incl. Reblochon, Abondance, Beaufort

name: Vosgienne
notes: Vosges Mountains; milk prized for AOC Munster; origin 17th century per Raveneau, disputed

name: Normande
notes: Normandy; early 1800s crossing with Durham/Shorthorn; herd-book 1883; high-fat milk for butter and cheese

name: Salers
notes: Cantal, Massif Central; milk for AOC Cantal and Salers

name: Dexter
notes: County Kerry; dual-purpose; about 2250 kg milk per lactation; breed society 1917

name: Kerry
notes: Rare Irish dairy breed; milk about 3000 to 3700 kg per lactation

name: Rhode Island Red
notes: Brown eggs; first shown under current name 1895; old-type hens 200 to 300 eggs a year

name: Welsummer
notes: Welsum; dark brown eggs; standard 1922-23

name: Light Sussex
notes: Light variety of Sussex; standard drawn up 1902; tinted eggs, about 180 to 200 a year

name: American Pekin
notes: Pekin ducks; from ducks taken from China, imported to US 1872-73; over 150 white eggs a year

name: Burford Brown
notes: Deep chestnut brown eggs; sold under Clarence Court; developed at Coach House Farm near Chipping Campden; association with Mabel Pearman

name: Old Cotswold Legbar
notes: Pastel blue, green and pinkish eggs; bred from Araucana hens; Clarence Court foundation bird; developed at Coach House Farm
